editionStatus: October 2018; still listed on the current AAST technical-guidelines index
authorityBoundary: Use for technologist transcutaneous-monitor setup, sensor application, calibration, signal-quality monitoring, troubleshooting, safety, treatment-monitoring context, and documentation. Current AASM Scoring Manual rules control hypoventilation definitions, thresholds, scoring, and required reporting. Keep TcCO2 and ETCO2 distinct because sensor behavior, lag, calibration, and artifacts differ.
bestFor: Transcutaneous CO2 monitoring during diagnostic and therapeutic PSG, equipment/sensor preparation, calibration, site and signal-quality considerations, troubleshooting, patient-safety considerations, treatment-response monitoring, and documentation.

mappingRationale.D2A: Supports equipment, sensor application, calibration, and technical preparation for transcutaneous CO2 monitoring.
mappingRationale.D2B: Supports performance of transcutaneous monitoring during diagnostic and therapeutic sleep testing.
mappingRationale.D2C: Supports calibration verification, troubleshooting, signal-quality response, safety awareness, and documentation.
mappingRationale.D3A: Supports valid CO2-signal context while AASM rules control adult scoring.
mappingRationale.D3B: Supports valid CO2-signal context while AASM rules control pediatric/infant scoring.
mappingRationale.D4C: Supports ventilation and CO2 monitoring context during oxygen or therapeutic interventions; oxygen administration remains order/facility-policy dependent.

copyrightUse: Use document title, section headings, original summaries, and learning objectives. Do not reproduce substantial procedures, figures, equipment illustrations, or superseded scoring thresholds.
